Analysis

Theme

The veto map flipped twice

The USSR cast most vetoes until 1960, the United States from the 1970s to the 1990s, Russia and China since 2011. 270 drafts have been vetoed since 1946.

What is veto power?

Decisions of the Security Council on anything beyond procedure need nine of the fifteen votes, and none of the five permanent members may vote against (Article 27 of the UN Charter). A single no vote from a permanent member therefore blocks a draft, however many members support it. That no vote is the veto. By long practice an abstention by a permanent member does not block adoption.

Which countries have veto power?

The five permanent members: China, France, Russia (the Soviet Union until December 1991), the United Kingdom and the United States. China's seat was held by the Republic of China (Taipei) until October 1971. The ten elected members have no veto.

Joint Russia and China vetoes

17 drafts were vetoed by Russia and China voting no together, all since 1972, newest first.
